what: Power Ministry orders Tata Mundra (CGPL, imported coal) to run at full capacity, 1 Apr–30 Jun; Maharashtra holds a supplementary PPA
Adani Power gets the letter of award for 2,500 MW renewable round-the-clock power, 25 years
State cabinet approves splitting MSEDCL and an IPO of the non-farm business
Largest cut of the period: 2,050 MW (6.1 MU that day)
All Koyna hydro machines stopped for low reservoir level; about 1,920 MW listed as fuel shortage in early June
Mundra full-capacity order extended to 30 Sep
1,850 MW cut between 20:00 and 21:00; reported causes include coal-quality derating at MAHAGENCO and outages at JSW, RattanIndia and Koradi
MSEDCL tenders 2,000 MW / 4,000 MWh of battery storage for 15 years
1,600 MW thermal PPA signed with Adani Power at Rs 5.30/kWh, supply from FY2030-31
State announces a Rs 48,000 crore waiver of farm power dues
MERC sets tariffs for 2,269 MW of farm-feeder solar (MSKVY 2.0) at Rs 2.24–2.90/kWh
RattanIndia Amravati Unit 5 (270 MW) out for coal shortage until about 27 Sep
Koyna dam full
Most energy cut in one day: 8.2 MU
2,500 MW round-the-clock PPA signed with PTSL (Adani trading arm) at Rs 5.90/kWh, supply from 28 Feb 2027
12 of 22 Maharashtra plants at critical coal stock; MAHAGENCO at 25.6% of requirement
Battery auction result: 1,500 MW at Rs 2.38 lakh/MW/month and 500 MW at Rs 2.40
Power Ministry orders 112 captive plants to run at maximum 1 Oct–31 Dec and sell surplus on exchanges; Mundra order extended to 31 Dec
MERC puts MSEDCL's request for 1,600 MW from NTPC Lara Stage III on hold pending the central allocation
15 of 20 Maharashtra plants at critical stock; MAHAGENCO at 19%, Tiroda at 6%
MSEDCL peak demand of 28,221 MW, highest this financial year
Maharashtra peak demand of 33,051 MW
MSEDCL official tells the press there has been no load shedding and that it is buying month-ahead power; SLDC reports show cuts on 11 days in October
